dense low-relief carving covering the whole field
glyph-like signs with rounded, cartouche-framed elements
framing border/edge band around the carved panel

justification: Both show a tall upright slab whose face is filled edge-to-edge with dense low relief in the same idiom: rounded cartouche-like blocks containing small faces or heads, framed by a raised border, suggesting a shared sign-and-relief convention. The biggest difference in content is that A depicts a single large elaborately costumed figure with a huge headdress and serpentine ornament dominating the field, whereas B shows only a regular double column grid of repeated square glyph blocks with no large figure (the man leaning on the monument is an onlooker, not part of the carving).
